answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust a slow, non-transferable work trail. A newcomer starts as a sparrow among established workers: it may take only small jobs, each one checked before the next unlocks, and its completed trail becomes a relic of proven work that cannot be copied or sold to another identity. Because the trail takes real calendar time and each step depends on the last, creating a hundred fakes buys no shortcut, and on the horizon the cost of forging a trusted history exceeds any reward from flooding the system.
